knowledge:
- key_parameters: i=The name of the assay in the QFeatures object to perform the operation on ;; robust=Logical (typically TRUE) in msqrob() to enable M-estimation for outlier robustness ;; fcol=The rowData column name used to group peptides/precursors into proteins (e.g., "Proteins" or "Protein.Group") in aggregateFeatures() ;; fun=The summarization method function passed to aggregateFeatures() (e.g., MsCoreUtils::medianPolish or iq::maxLFQ) ;; pNA=The maximum allowed proportion of missing values (NAs) for a feature to be retained in filterNA()
- alternatives: MsCoreUtils::medianPolish (with na.rm = TRUE) can be used as a faster alternative to default robust summarization or iq::maxLFQ in aggregateFeatures() for large datasets ;; QFeatures::normalize can be used instead of sweep with nfLogMedian for normalization ;; Imputation via QFeatures::impute can be performed, though msqrob2 is designed to handle missing data directly without imputation
- when_to_use: Use when performing differential abundance analysis on label-free quantitative (LFQ) proteomics data (DDA or DIA) where robust handling of outliers, peptide-specific effects, and missing values is required
- pitfalls: readQFeatures does not process 64-bit integers correctly, so integer64 = "double" must be specified when reading text files with data.table::fread ;; Missing values must be explicitly encoded as NA using zeroIsNA before log-transformation ;; MsCoreUtils::medianPolish cannot handle missing values by default, so na.rm = TRUE must be explicitly passed when using it ;; Robust summarization and maxLFQ can be computationally expensive and slow for large datasets

workflows.name: dda_maxquant_peptide_workflow
workflows.intent: Analyze MaxQuant DDA peptide-level data to identify differentially abundant proteins.
input: peptides.txt (MaxQuant peptide-level intensity table in wide format)
experimental_design.csv (sample annotation table mapping quantification columns to experimental conditions)
workflows.stages: 1. Import peptide table and sample annotations ;; 2. Convert to QFeatures object using readQFeatures ;; 3. Replace zeros with NA using zeroIsNA ;; 4. Log2-transform intensities using logTransform ;; 5. Filter out failed protein inferences, shared peptides, decoys, and contaminants using filterFeatures ;; 6. Filter out highly missing peptides using filterNA ;; 7. Normalize intensities using sweep and nfLogMedian ;; 8. Summarize peptide intensities to protein level using aggregateFeatures ;; 9. Fit robust linear models using msqrob ;; 10. Define contrasts using makeContrast and perform hypothesis testing using hypothesisTest ;; 11. Collect results using msqrobCollect and visualize using plotVolcano
workflows.code:
peptides <- data.table::fread(peptideFile, check.names = TRUE, integer64 = "double")
quantCols <- grep("Intensity[.]", names(peptides), value = TRUE)
(annot <- data.frame(quantCols = quantCols) |>
mutate(sampleId = gsub("Intensity[.]6","", quantCols),
condition = substr(sampleId,1,1),
rep = substr(sampleId, 3, 3))
)
(qf <- readQFeatures(assayData = peptides, colData = annot, name = "peptides", fnames = "Sequence") )
qf <- zeroIsNA(qf, "peptides")
qf <- logTransform(qf, base = 2, i = "peptides", name = "peptides_log")
qf <- filterFeatures(
 qf, ~ Proteins != "" &
 !grepl(";", Proteins))
qf <- filterFeatures(qf, ~ Reverse != "+" &
 Potential.contaminant != "+")
nObs <- 3
n <- ncol(qf[["peptides_log"]])
(qf <- filterNA(qf, i = "peptides_log", pNA = (n - nObs) / n))
qf <- sweep(
qf, MARGIN = 2, STATS = nfLogMedian(qf,"peptides_log"), i = "peptides_log", name = "peptides_norm"
)
qf <- aggregateFeatures(qf, i = "peptides_norm", fcol = "Proteins", na.rm = TRUE, name = "proteins"
)
model <- ~ condition
qf <- msqrob(
 qf, i = "proteins", formula = model, robust = TRUE)
(L <- makeContrast(
 "conditionB = 0", parameterNames = colnames(vd$designmatrix)
))
qf <- hypothesisTest(qf, i = "proteins", contrast = L)
inferences <- msqrobCollect(qf[["proteins"]], L)
inferences |> plotVolcano()

workflows.name: dia_precursor_workflow
workflows.intent: Analyze DIA precursor-level data (from DIA-NN or Spectronaut) to identify differentially abundant proteins.
input: report.parquet (DIA-NN or Spectronaut precursor-level quantification table in long format)
experimental_design.csv (sample annotation table mapping runs to experimental conditions)
workflows.stages: 1. Import precursor table and sample annotations ;; 2. Convert long-format precursor table to QFeatures object using readQFeatures ;; 3. Replace zeros with NA using zeroIsNA ;; 4. Filter out questionable identifications, decoys, and non-proteotypic peptides using filterFeatures ;; 5. Join run-specific assays into a single precursor assay using joinAssays ;; 6. Filter out highly missing precursors using filterNA ;; 7. Filter out "one-hit wonder" proteins (proteins with only one peptide) using filterFeatures ;; 8. Log2-transform intensities using logTransform ;; 9. Normalize intensities using sweep and nfLogMedian ;; 10. Summarize precursor intensities to protein level using aggregateFeatures with maxLFQ or medianPolish ;; 11. Fit robust linear models using msqrob ;; 12. Generate pairwise contrasts using createPairwiseContrasts and makeContrast ;; 13. Perform hypothesis testing using hypothesisTest ;; 14. Collect results using msqrobCollect and visualize using plotVolcano
workflows.code:
precursors <- arrow::read_parquet(precursorFile)
(annot <- data.frame(runCol = precursors |> pull(Run) |> unique()
) |>
mutate(sampleId = gsub(x = runCol, pattern = "_DIA", replacement = "") |>
str_split("UPS2_") |>
sapply(`[`, 2)
) |>
mutate(
 condition = gsub("ratio", "", sampleId) |>
 str_split("_") |>
 sapply(`[`, 1) |>
 as.numeric() |>
 as.factor(),
 rep = sampleId |>
 str_split("_") |>
 sapply(`[`, 2) |>
 replace_na(replace = "1") |>
 as.factor(),
 ratio = condition |>
 as.character() |>
 as.double()
) )
(qf <- readQFeatures(assayData = precursors, colData = annot, quantCols = "Precursor.Quantity", runCol = "Run", fnames = "Precursor.Id"))
qf <- zeroIsNA(qf, names(qf))
qf <- qf |>
 filterFeatures(~ Q.Value <= 0.01 &
 PG.Q.Value <= 0.01 &
 Lib.Q.Value <= 0.01 &
 Lib.PG.Q.Value <= 0.01 &
 Precursor.Id != "" &
 Decoy == 0 &
 Proteotypic == 1)
(qf <- joinAssays(
 x = qf,
 i = names(qf),
 fcol = "Precursor.Id",
 name = "precursors"
))
nObs <- 4
n <- ncol(qf[["precursors"]])
(qf <- filterNA(qf, i = "precursors", pNA = (n - nObs) / n))
pepsPerProtDf <- qf[["precursors"]] |>
 rowData() |>
 data.frame() |>
 dplyr::select("Stripped.Sequence", "Protein.Group") |>
 group_by(Protein.Group) |>
 mutate(pepsPerProt = Stripped.Sequence |>
 unique() |>
 length()
 )
rowData(qf[["precursors"]])$pepsPerProt <- pepsPerProtDf$pepsPerProt
qf <- filterFeatures(qf, ~ pepsPerProt > 1, keep = TRUE)
qf <- logTransform(qf, base = 2, i = "precursors", name = "precursors_log")
qf <- sweep(
qf, MARGIN = 2, STATS = nfLogMedian(qf,"precursors_log"), i = "precursors_log", name = "precursors_norm"
)
(qf <- aggregateFeatures(
 qf,
 i = "precursors_norm",
 name = "proteins",
 fcol = "Protein.Group",
 fun = function(X) iq::maxLFQ(X)$estimate
))
model <- ~ condition
qf <- msqrob(
 qf, i = "proteins", formula = model, robust = TRUE)
(allHypotheses <- createPairwiseContrasts(
 model,
 colData(qf),
 "condition"
) )
(L <- makeContrast(
 allHypotheses,
 parameterNames = colnames(vd$designmatrix)
))
qf <- hypothesisTest(qf, i = "proteins", contrast = L)
inferences <- msqrobCollect(qf[["proteins"]], L)
volcanoplots <- inferences |> plotVolcano() + facet_wrap(~contrast)
